code: treatment <- OBrienKaiser$treatment do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(treatment), function(g) {   res <- typicality_geom(effect[treatment == g, ], point = c(0, 0), seed = 1)   data.frame(group = g, n = res$n,              D = round(res$statistic, 2),              p_value = round(res$p_value, 4),              notable = res$notable) })) #>     group n    D p_value notable #> 1 control 5 0.15  1.0000   FALSE #> 2       A 4 7.91  0.1250    TRUE #> 3       B 7 2.06  0.0312    TRUE res_control <- typicality_geom(effect[treatment == "control", ], point = c(0, 0)) res_treated <- typicality_geom(effect[treatment %in% c("A", "B"), ],                                point = c(0, 0), seed = 1) res_treated #>  #> Geometric typicality test (mean point) #> -------------------------------------- #> Cloud           : n = 11 points, dimensionality L = 2 #> Reference point : (0; 0) #>  #> Mahalanobis distance D = 2.067  -- notable deviation #> Test statistic d2_obs  = 0.8103 #> Distribution    : exact (exhaustive enumeration), 1,024 samples #> p-value         : 4 / 2,048 = 0.001953 #> 95% compatibility : principal kappa-ellipsoid, kappa = 0.9828 plot(res_treated)

title: Combinatorial typicality testing on an MCA: a tutorial
text: use hdv2003 questionr (2000 respondents French “Histoire de vie” survey) seven yes/cultural leisure practices. build standard MCA FactoMineR, adding sexe occup (activity status) supplementary variables age supplementary numeric variable, shape cloud can located . first plane (axes 1–2) carries main structure, read typicality tests . (MCA’s raw inertia rates notoriously pessimistic; matters geometry plane, percentages.)
code: library(GDAinference) library(FactoMineR) library(ggplot2) data("hdv2003", package = "questionr")  active <- c("hard.rock", "lecture.bd", "peche.chasse",             "cuisine", "bricol", "cinema", "sport") d <- hdv2003[, c(active, "sexe", "occup", "age")]  mca <- MCA(d, quali.sup = 8:9, quanti.sup = 10, ncp = Inf, graph = FALSE) round(mca$eig[1:3, ], 2) #>       eigenvalue percentage of variance cumulative percentage of variance #> dim 1       0.21                  21.22                             21.22 #> dim 2       0.15                  15.43                             36.65 #> dim 3       0.15                  14.68                             51.33

title: Combinatorial typicality testing on an MCA: a tutorial
text: testing anything, must understand axes mean — otherwise p-value just number. map shows active categories (grey) activity-status groups (orange).  Two clear oppositions emerge: Axis 1 — volume practices. right sit “Oui” categories (hard.rock, lecture.bd, sport, cinema); left, “Non” categories. right means many things, left . supplementary variable age correlates −0.44 axis: older respondents left (fewer practices), younger right. Axis 2 — kind practice. top, outdoor/manual leisure (peche.chasse stands , bricol); bottom, urban-cultural leisure (lecture.bd, cinema, hard.rock). orange occupation points already tell story: students sit far lower right (young, many urban-cultural practices), retired people left (older, fewer practices), employed unemployed sit close centre. Typicality testing turns visual impression formal statement.
code: cats <- function(coord, type) {   df <- as.data.frame(coord[, 1:2]); names(df) <- c("D1", "D2")   data.frame(label = rownames(df), D1 = df$D1, D2 = df$D2, type = type) } map <- rbind(   cats(mca$var$coord, "leisure category"),   cats(mca$quali.sup$coord[levels(hdv2003$occup), ], "occupation") )  ggplot(map, aes(D1, D2, colour = type, label = label)) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey85") +   geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey85") +   geom_point(size = 1.6) +   # thin out the leisure labels, but always show the (few) occupation labels   geom_text(data = subset(map, type == "leisure category"),             size = 2.8, vjust = -0.7, check_overlap = TRUE, show.legend = FALSE) +   geom_text(data = subset(map, type == "occupation"),             size = 3, fontface = "bold", vjust = -0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c("leisure category" = "grey45",                                  "occupation" = "#D95F02")) +   scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.18)) +   scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.08)) +   coord_equal(clip = "off") + theme_minimal() +   labs(x = "Axis 1 (volume of practices)",        y = "Axis 2 (outdoor vs. urban-cultural)", colour = NULL)

title: Combinatorial Inference in Geometric Data Analysis
text: Run GDA, ask whether group atypical cloud: second test, geometric typicality (ch. 4), asks instead whether cloud’s mean point coincides fixed reference point (e.g. origin), using sign-flip permutation cloud’s covariance: third test, homogeneity (ch. 5), compares mean points two groups: differ? Either within whole cloud (comparison = "partial", default) restricting cloud groups (comparison = "specific"): two groups statistic Mahalanobis distance mean points (compatibility region); two -group Mahalanobis variance (omnibus test). calls work GDAtools speMCA / csMCA ade4 dudi.pca / dudi.acm object — just pass instead. See vignette("typicality", "GDAinference") full walk-read results (notably, significant vs. notable).
code: library(GDAinference) library(FactoMineR) data(hdv2003, package = "questionr")   # 2000 respondents, French "Histoire de vie" survey  # A standard MCA of seven leisure practices, with activity status (occup) # added as a supplementary variable -- the usual GDA workflow: vars <- c("hard.rock", "lecture.bd", "peche.chasse", "cuisine",           "bricol", "cinema", "sport") mca <- MCA(hdv2003[, c(vars, "occup")], quali.sup = 8, graph = FALSE)  # Is the mean point of each activity-status group atypical? (first plane) typicality_byvar(mca, "occup", axes = 1:2, seed = 1) #> Combinatorial typicality test by category of 'occup' #> Cloud: n = 2000 individuals, dimensionality L = 2 #> #>               category  n_c     D p_value sig notable #>  Exerce une profession 1049 0.279   0.000   *      no   # significant, but D < 0.4 (large n) #>                Chomeur  134 0.129   0.305          no   # compatible with the whole cloud #>        Etudiant, eleve   94 0.973   0.000   *     yes   # strongly atypical #>               Retraite  392 0.537   0.000   *     yes #>    Retire des affaires   77 0.679   0.000   *     yes #>               Au foyer  171 0.388   0.000   *      no #>          Autre inactif   83 0.762   0.000   *     yes #> #> * p <= 0.05   |   'notable': D >= 0.4   |   montecarlo  # Test a single group and visualise its 95% compatibility region: res <- typicality_comb(mca, group = "occup", level = "Etudiant, eleve", axes = 1:2) plot(res) # Are the students located at the cloud's origin, or genuinely displaced? typicality_geom(mca, group = "occup", level = "Etudiant, eleve",                 point = 0, axes = 1:2) # Do students and the retired occupy different positions in the first plane? res <- homogeneity(mca, group = "occup",                    groups = c("Etudiant, eleve", "Retraite"), axes = 1:2) res plot(res)   # the deviation Gc2 - Gc1 against its 95% compatibility region  # Omit `groups` to test all categories at once (global omnibus): are the # activity-status groups heterogeneous overall? homogeneity(mca, group = "occup", axes = 1:2)

(2019), chapter 5: three groups of the # 10-point cloud (groups i7, i8 pooled into group 3, giving sizes 3, 2, 5). grp <- c(1, 1, 3, 3, 3, 1, 3, 3, 2, 2) homogeneity(Target, grp, groups = c(1, 2))                # two groups: p = 1/2520 #>  #> Combinatorial homogeneity test (two groups) #> ------------------------------------------- #> Cloud           : n = 10 points, dimensionality L = 2 #> Comparison      : partial -- "1" (n1 = 3) vs "2" (n2 = 2), others pooled (n_r = 5) #>  #> Proportion of variance (eta^2) = 0.5399  -- notable difference #> Mahalanobis distance D = 2.735  (D^2 = 7.479) between the mean points #> Distribution    : exact (exhaustive enumeration), 2,520 arrangements #> p-value         : 1 / 2,520 = 0.0003968 #> 95% compatibility : principal kappa-ellipsoid, kappa = 3.356 homogeneity(Target, grp, groups = c(1, 2), comparison = "specific")  # 2/10 #>  #> Combinatorial homogeneity test (two groups) #> ------------------------------------------- #> Cloud           : n = 5 points, dimensionality L = 2 #> Comparison      : global -- "1" (n1 = 3) vs "2" (n2 = 2) #>  #> Proportion of variance (eta^2) = 0.6976  -- notable difference #> Mahalanobis distance D = 2.004  (D^2 = 4.014) between the mean points #> Distribution    : exact (exhaustive enumeration), 10 arrangements #> p-value         : 2 / 10 = 0.2 #> 95% compatibility : Finite compatibility region is not accessible. homogeneity(Target, grp)        # global omnibus of the three groups: p = 37/2520 #>  #> Combinatorial homogeneity test (3 groups) #> ----------------------------------------- #> Cloud           : n = 10 points, dimensionality L = 2 #> Comparison      : global -- 3 groups: "1" (3), "2" (2), "3" (5) #>  #> Proportion of variance (eta^2) = 0.5833  -- notable difference #> Between-group M-variance V_M = 1.001 #> Distribution    : exact (exhaustive enumeration), 2,520 arrangements #> p-value         : 37 / 2,520 = 0.01468

title: GDAinference 0.0.0.9000 (development version)
text: Initial scaffolding package. get_coord(): compatibility layer extracting principal coordinates matrices/data frames FactoMineR, GDAtools ade4 result objects. typicality_comb(): exact combinatorial typicality test mean point (Le Roux, Bienaise & Durand 2019, ch. 3), print()/summary() methods 95% compatibility ellipsoid. Reproduces book’s “Target” example (D = 0.964, p = 9/210). typicality_geom(): geometric (sign-flip) typicality test mean point reference point (Le Roux, Bienaise & Durand 2019, ch. 4), print() plot() methods. Handles multidimensional case (κ-ellipse compatibility region), one-dimensional case (one-sided p-value exact compatibility interval) optional restriction subgroup. Reproduces book’s Target example (D = 0.964, p = 86/1024, κ ≈ 1.08) Student example (one-sided p = 1/512, interval [0.833, 2.467]). homogeneity(): exact combinatorial homogeneity test (Le Roux, Bienaise & Durand 2019, ch. 5), print() plot() methods. Compares mean points two groups (groups, categories group global comparison), partial comparison (groups within whole cloud) specific comparison (cloud restricted groups). two groups statistic squared Mahalanobis distance D²_M two mean points, compatibility region (principal κ-ellipsoid two dimensions; signed one-sided test exact compatibility interval one dimension); two groups - group Mahalanobis variance V_M (omnibus test, region). proportion-- variance (partial η²) descriptive index always reported. Reproduces book’s Target example (two-group partial p = 1/2520, κ ≈ 3.36; specific p = 2/10; global three-group omnibus p = 37/2520). plot() methods test results, drawn ggplot2: typicality, cloud centre, group mean compatibility ellipse; homogeneity, observed deviation compatibility region. typicality_comb() gains level argument, group can named category supplementary/grouping variable (vector, variable name stored GDA result, e.g. FactoMineR quali.sup). typicality_byvar(): run test every category variable , returning tidy table (multidimensional, exact counterpart GDAtools’ dimtypicality()). Tutorial vignette “Combinatorial typicality testing MCA” — full worked example questionr::hdv2003 (FactoMineR MCA), cloud interpretation, plots guidance reading tests (notably distinction significant notable deviation). Tutorial vignette “Geometric typicality: testing effect principal plane” — worked GDA example book’s Parkinson study (§6.1): PCA O’Brien–Kaiser repeated-measures response profiles, geometric typicality test →effect-vectors first principal plane, contrasting treated group (atypical effect) control group (compatible effect). Compatibility documented backed integration tests: formally tested FactoMineR (PCA, MCA), GDAtools (speMCA, csMCA) ade4 (dudi.pca, dudi.acm); similarly-structured GDA objects expected work yet formally tested. Bundled example data sets: Target, Target_group, Student.
